title: From the House of Yemanjá
author: Audre Lorde
source: The Black Unicorn: Poems (1978) / W.W. Norton & Company
citation: Lorde, Audre. 'From the House of Yemanjá.' The Black Unicorn: Poems, W.W. Norton & Company, 1978, pp. 6–7.

sections.heading: From the House of Yemanjá (Complete Poem)

epigraph.quote: I bear two women upon my back / one dark and rich and hidden... the other bright and ivory / standing in the sun.

paragraphs:
My mother had two faces and a pot of fire
with which she burned away all my impurities
and made me over into her own image
the image of a woman who never smiled
and whose tongue was like a razor.

I bear two women upon my back
one dark and rich and hidden
in the secret places of my heart
the other bright and ivory
standing in the sun.

All this has been
before in my dreams
the two women fighting for my soul
and my mother watching from the shadows
waiting to see which one would conquer.

Mother I need
mother I need
your blackness now as before
and your strength
to fight the cold.

There is never enough night
there is never enough dark
to hide all the sorrows
of the women who gave me birth.
